subject: POC planning follow-up / workload profile for Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: POC next steps & workload profile (Acme Health)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned: 

TL;DR: Acme wants to validate latency and cost for your triage assistant use case with a 2-week POC. Success criteria and an evaluation plan are below. Can you confirm the workload numbers and owners by EOD tomorrow?

Recap from the call:
- Goal: Replace rule-based triage with ML assistant for intake + routing (English clinical forms).
- Key success criteria you mentioned: 95th percentile latency < 600ms for single-turn queries, average per-call token cost < $0.035, and F1 > 0.88 on your labeled triage set.
- Timeline: hope to run a 2-week trial starting 5/10; decision meeting week of 5/24.

Proposed evaluation plan (suggested):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize scope and workload profile (RPS and token distribution).
2) Week 1-2 (5/10-5/23): run POC on Redwood Dedicated dev pool (identical infra as prod), collect latency/cost/quality metrics, and log traces for top-10 slowest requests.
3) Post-POC: extend with canary to 10% traffic for 2 weeks if metrics pass.

Workload intake fields we need filled (please confirm the numbers in bold or correct them):
- Peak RPS (sustained): 20 rps
- Typical RPS (sustained): 6 rps
- Burst pattern: periodic 30-45s spikes up to 120 rps for short windows (5-10s) during clinician shifts
- Avg prompt length: 420 tokens (user + system + context)
- Avg completion length: 140 tokens
- 95th percentile token length: 1,200 tokens
- Concurrent conversations: 150 active sessions (KV cache affinity per session)
- Expected test data size: ~3k labeled items for quality eval

Owners / next steps:
- Acme owner to confirm workload numbers and provide sample sanitized logs: Alex + Sara
- Redwood owner to produce POC plan and environment access: Ben (engineering lead)
- Success criteria doc attached for your edits (poc_success_criteria_template.docx).

If those workload numbers look off, flag the fields you want adjusted and share any sample payloads (sanitized). Happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: poc_success_criteria_template.docx

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC next steps & workload profile (Acme Health)

Thanks Marissa — this is great, appreciate the clear plan. Confirming the numbers and adding a few clarifications: 

- Peak RPS (sustained): 20 rps — confirmed.
- Typical RPS (sustained): 6 rps — confirmed.
- Burst pattern: We see predictable bursts at shift changes and morning syncs. Spikes up to 120 rps are accurate but they are very short (3-8s).
- Avg prompt length: 380 tokens (we trimmed templates after the call) — please use 380 as the avg.
- Avg completion length: 160 tokens — slight bump expected for edge cases.
- 95th percentile token length: ~1,100 tokens — current cap at 1,200 is safe.
- Concurrent conversations: 110 active sessions typically, 150 is possible during business-critical days — use 150 for sizing.
- Test data: we can provide 3,200 labeled items.

Owners: Alex (PM) + Sara (platform eng) — I'll upload sample sanitized logs to the Drive link you shared by EOD tomorrow.

One more ask: can Redwood provide recommended initial instance sizing / expected cost estimate for the 2-week run? Would like a ballpark to share with finance.

Best,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Product Manager, Clinical Automation
Acme Health

Forwarded attachment: sample_payloads.json (see Drive)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: POC next steps & workload profile (Acme Health)

Thanks for the forward — taking lead on sizing and cost. Initial recommendation for the 2-week POC: 

Suggested infra (dev-dedicated pool):
- Instance type: 2 x A40 equivalent GPUs per node (NVLink offload not required for this model).
- Nodes: 3 nodes (6 GPUs total). Rationale: handles sustained 20 rps with headroom for 150 concurrent sessions + short bursts; continuous batching to keep per-token cost low.
- Autoscale policy: allow burst capacity up to 8 nodes for short windows (5-10s) with warm standby; fallback policy to smaller model variant if capacity limits reached.

Estimated cost (2-week run, inclusive of infra + streaming): ~$12k-$18k (ballpark; final depends on actual token counts during run). We'll produce a more precise estimate after we get sample payloads.

Eval dashboard (we'll ship a shared Grafana link):
- Metrics: per-call latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens per call, per-call cost, top slow traces, error rate, throughput (rps), and quality scores against their labeled set (F1/precision/recall).

Next steps: 
1) Acme uploads sanitized logs & labeled set (Alex).
2) Redwood infra team (Dylan) prepares a dev-dedicated pool and provisioning playbook.
3) I will draft the POC runbook and kickoff email to schedule environment access by 5/7.

I'll prepare the cost breakdown and a brief runbook today and share it in this thread.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
